_meta.description: D6 fixtures for google-antigravity / tool-rendering. Owns the FIVE tool-rendering suggestion pills ("What's the weather in San Francisco?", "Find flights from SFO to JFK.", "What's the current price of AAPL?", "Roll a 20-sided die.", "Chain a few tools in this single turn: ...") for the whole tool-rendering family — the default-catchall and custom-catchall pages ship the same four prompts and are served from here, so neither of those files may carry a duplicate copy (they load first alphabetically and would shadow these).
_meta.googleAntigravityStaging: google-antigravity staging: the Antigravity Go harness owns the conversation history and never sends role:"tool" messages -- a completed tool call comes back as an assistant message whose text is 'Tool response for <name>: ...'. hasToolResult/toolCallId therefore never fire here, so every leg is staged on turnIndex (aimock's count of assistant messages; +2 per tool round-trip, +1 per text answer). turnIndex is a POSITION disambiguator, not a reject gate (aimock selectByTurnIndex): the candidate with the highest turnIndex <= assistantCount wins, so a leg must carry EVERY absolute position a test can reach it from -- a fresh thread (0/2) AND its slot in a multi-pill single-thread sequence.

fixtures._comment: tool-rendering pill 'Roll a d20' — exactly FIVE sequential roll_d20 calls returning [7, 14, 3, 19, 20], then a closing text. The chain used to be linked by toolCallId, which cannot work here (no role:"tool" messages, and the adapter mints its own uuid for every server-tool call anyway), so each roll is pinned to an absolute turnIndex. Two interleaved chains are scripted because the specs reach this pill from two positions and the two ladders never collide: a fresh thread walks the EVEN counts 0/2/4/6/8 (text at 10) and the 'sequential pills in one thread' test, which clicks Find flights first, walks the ODD counts 3/5/7/9/11 (text at 13). Both ladders yield exactly 5 cards with 20 last.

fixtures._comment: Shared d5-tool-rendering probe prompt (ONE user turn). leg 1: emit get_weather(Tokyo). BOTH gates are load-bearing. `toolName` keeps the leg out of requests from agents that do not declare get_weather — the shared smoke probe's `tools:` row sends "What is the weather in Tokyo?" to an agent whose tool list is ['manage_task','schedule'], and without the gate the harness aborted the run with `unknown_tool: get_weather` (measured). `turnIndex: 0` pins the POSITION: an untagged leg is eligible at every position and beats an equal-position scripted leg registered after it, which let this fixture answer the 'Chain tools' pill's second turn (that pill's prompt contains the substring 'weather in Tokyo').

A quantum computer uses qubits, which can sit in a fuzzy superposition of both states at once until you check them.
